Subject: PoC trial plan: deployment mode decision (Hosted | Dedicated | Private) — Acme Corp

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the deep dive on Acme's expected load patterns and compliance needs. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can lock the PoC scope and timeline: 

Summary of needs (from your team):
- Predictable low-latency generation for interactive tooling (~ <200ms p95 for 512 tokens)
- Strict data isolation for PII-sensitive flows (audit logs; customer data never persist beyond session)
- Run an initial pilot with representative traffic (peak ~150 qps, average 20 qps)

Deployment modes we're evaluating:
- Hosted API: fastest to start, shared infra, usage-based pricing
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and isolation (recommended for steady 100+ qps)
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for full network control and on-prem compliance (longer lead time)

Proposed PoC / trial plan (attach: PoC-scope.xlsx):
1) Baseline week (Week 0): Redwood runs a short baseline on Hosted to validate model parity and token costs.
2) Performance pilot (Weeks 1–3): spin up a Dedicated trial pool to measure latency/throughput under your load; we’ll run representative traffic and KV/prompt cache scenarios.
3) Security review (parallel): Redwood provides SOC2 evidence and network topology doc; your security team does an audit.
4) Success criteria (mutually agreed): p95 latency <200ms at 75% of target qps, no data persistence beyond session, error rate <1% under load, cost per 1k tokens within agreed threshold.

Requested decisions from Acme for kickoff:
- Preferred deployment mode to prioritize for the PoC (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) -> please confirm.
- Pilot timeline constraints and key stakeholders (SRE, Security, Product).
- Any legal/docs we should prep (NDA, SOC2 evidence requests, DPA).

Next steps I propose:
- If you prefer Dedicated, we can provision a 2-week reserved trial (no upfront commitment) and run load tests.
- I'll attach a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for signatures to lock timeline and responsibilities.
- Weekly 30-min sync during the PoC; kickoff as soon as stakeholders confirmed.

Attachments: PoC-scope.xlsx (scope & test matrix), MAP-MutualActionPlan.pdf (draft)

Would you confirm which mode you want to prioritize and availability for a 30-min kickoff next week?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical note from the infra side following Ben's recap.

Thanks for laying out the traffic profile — from an ops/perf perspective, Dedicated capacity is the cleanest path to guarantee p95 latency under consistent high qps. A few practical notes:
- Dedicated allows us to pin GPU instances and pre-warm KV caches for your test prompts, which materially reduces tail latency for sessions with long context.
- If Acme wants eventual Private (VPC) for compliance, we can run the same tests inside a Private trial, but setup typically adds ~2–4 weeks for networking & KMS integrations.
- For the PoC, we recommend the following bill of materials: 2x A100-equivalent reserved pods (for redundancy) + a lightweight autoscaler to simulate bursts.

What we can deliver during the pilot:
- A performance report: per-route latency distribution, token-level cost breakdown, trace samples.
- A security packet: SOC2 excerpt and data handling notes (see attached SOC2-prior-art.pdf).
- Help with a test harness (we can share a small load generator script and synthetic prompts).

If Acme confirms Dedicated as the first pass, I can provision the trial pool and share credentials for your SRE to run tests.

- Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks Ben & Marissa — this is helpful.

Acme's initial preference is to validate Dedicated capacity for the PoC. The reasons are primarily around predictable latency and avoiding noisy-neighbor variability while we exercise the product with synthetic traffic.

Our success criteria (high-level):
- p95 latency < 200ms for typical 512-token responses at 75% of expected peak qps
- End-to-end error rate <1% during test windows
- Clear audit trail for requests (session IDs, retention policy)
- Security review completed without blockers (SOC2 review + network diagram)

Timeline constraints: we are aiming to complete the pilot in ~3 weeks so we can brief execs in the first week of April. Stakeholders:
- Liam O'Connor (Product lead)
- Priya Singh (Head of Security)
- SRE: Alex Moreno (will be on the kickoff invite)

Items for Redwood:
- Confirmation you can provision a Dedicated trial pool that supports ~150 qps peak (2x reserved pods as suggested).
- SOC2 artifacts and DPA draft; if you have a standard DPA we can start the review.
- A short MAP so we can sign and lock dates.

Kickoff availability: Wed 18 Mar, 10:00am PT works for our core team.

Thanks — Liam
